title: DefectDojo
description: DefectDojo 3.5.103 (chart 1.9.69): Django/uwsgi behind nginx, Celery worker and beat, Valkey broker, PostgreSQL defectdojo-db (CloudNativePG). DefectDojo publishes no dashboard: built from the django-prometheus, nginx-prometheus-exporter and redis_exporter metric documentation. Sources: docs/dashboards/security.md

panels.description: How to read this dashboard.

options.content:
### DefectDojo: vulnerability management
**What it does here.** DefectDojo 3.5.103 (chart 1.9.69) at `defectdojo.<domain>`: pod `defectdojo-django` = **nginx** (front, static files) + **uwsgi** (Django app; 1 process × 4 threads once the metrics change is synced) + nginx-prometheus-exporter; **celery-worker** (imports, deduplication, notifications) and **celery-beat** (schedules) through **Valkey** (the Celery broker); PostgreSQL is the CloudNativePG cluster `defectdojo-db`.

**Healthy looks like:** everything UP, no 5xx, Celery queue at 0 (or draining), DB query p95 in milliseconds. Request panels count real users, the login page probes and the metrics scrape itself (left out where noted). Celery workers export no metrics: the queue depth in Valkey and the worker/beat Deployments are the signals.

**When something is red:** `kubectl --context k8s01 -n defectdojo logs deploy/defectdojo-django -c uwsgi` (or `-c nginx`, `deploy/defectdojo-celery-worker`); database → **CloudNativePG** dashboard (Databases folder, cluster `defectdojo-db`). Docs: [django-prometheus metrics](https://github.com/korfuri/django-prometheus/blob/master/documentation/metrics.md), `docs/dashboards/security.md`.

panels.title: Active alerts for this service
panels.description: Prometheus alerts of this service that are FIRING (condition true for longer than the rule's `for`) or PENDING (condition true, waiting for `for`). Same filter as the red alert annotations of this dashboard; Watchdog/InfoInhibitor are excluded. Empty = healthy. Alertmanager has no receiver in this lab, so dashboards are where alerts are seen: the rule, its threshold and source are in the rule files (helm-charts/<app>/**/prometheus.rules.yaml or the -raw release) and in docs/dashboards/. All alerts of the lab: dashboard "Alerts overview" (Observability folder).

panels.title: Django (uwsgi)
panels.description: Scrape of /django_metrics/metrics through nginx (basic auth, via the Service name): 1 = Django answers. Source: Prometheus up.

panels.title: nginx
panels.description: nginx_up: the exporter sidecar could read nginx stub_status (DefectDojoNginxDown after 5 min). Source: nginx-prometheus-exporter README (https://github.com/nginx/nginx-prometheus-exporter#metrics-for-nginx-oss)

panels.title: Valkey (broker)
panels.description: redis_up: the exporter reached Valkey (DefectDojoValkeyDown after 1 min, awesome-prometheus-alerts (https://github.com/samber/awesome-prometheus-alerts) 'Redis down'). Source: redis_exporter (oliver006/redis_exporter v1.93.0, metrics from Valkey INFO).

panels.title: PostgreSQL
panels.description: cnpg_collector_up of defectdojo-db (1 = PostgreSQL answers the CloudNativePG exporter). Details: CloudNativePG dashboard.

panels.title: Celery worker / beat
panels.description: Available replicas of the Celery Deployments (kube-state-metrics); 1 each expected. Workers have no metrics endpoint.

panels.title: HTTP 5xx (5m)
panels.description: Share of Django responses with a 5xx status over 5 min, the DefectDojoHighHttp5xxErrorRate expression: red at 5 % (awesome-prometheus-alerts (https://github.com/samber/awesome-prometheus-alerts) 'Nginx high HTTP 5xx error rate', applied to django-prometheus). 0 while no 5xx series exists; empty = no traffic. Source: django-prometheus documentation/metrics.md (https://github.com/korfuri/django-prometheus/blob/master/documentation/metrics.md)

panels.title: Celery queue
panels.description: Tasks waiting in the Celery default queue: length of the Valkey list `celery`, exported by redis_exporter (REDIS_EXPORTER_CHECK_SINGLE_KEYS=db0=celery, set in helm-charts/defectdojo). Celery deletes the list when it is empty, so no value = nothing queued. PENDING SCRAPE until that change is synced.

panels.title: Responses by status
panels.description: Django responses/s by HTTP status, including the metrics scrape and probes. Source: django_http_responses_total_by_status_total, django-prometheus documentation/metrics.md (https://github.com/korfuri/django-prometheus/blob/master/documentation/metrics.md)

panels.title: Requests by view (top 10)
panels.description: Requests/s per Django view name (url name), the metrics scrape view left out. `login` includes the kubelet probes. Source: django_http_requests_total_by_view_transport_method_total, django-prometheus documentation/metrics.md (https://github.com/korfuri/django-prometheus/blob/master/documentation/metrics.md)

panels.title: Latency p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: End-to-end request time inside Django including middlewares, histogram django_http_requests_latency_including_middlewares_seconds (same quantiles as the django-prometheus example recording rules, examples/prometheus/django.rules). Source: django-prometheus documentation/metrics.md (https://github.com/korfuri/django-prometheus/blob/master/documentation/metrics.md)

panels.title: Slowest views (p95)
panels.description: 95th percentile per view and method from django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method (top 10). Imports (`import_scan_results`, API `importscan`) are the expected slow ones. Source: django-prometheus documentation/metrics.md (https://github.com/korfuri/django-prometheus/blob/master/documentation/metrics.md)

targets.expr: topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, view, method) (rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_bucket{job="defectdojo-django", view!="prometheus-django-metrics"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: Exceptions by type
panels.description: Unhandled exceptions/s raised by views, by exception class. The series exist only after the first exception since uwsgi started (empty = none). Source: django_http_exceptions_total_by_type_total, django-prometheus documentation/metrics.md (https://github.com/korfuri/django-prometheus/blob/master/documentation/metrics.md)

panels.title: Connections
panels.description: nginx stub_status connection states: active (all open), reading (request headers), writing (sending responses, includes waits on uwsgi), waiting (idle keep-alive). Source: nginx-prometheus-exporter README (https://github.com/nginx/nginx-prometheus-exporter#metrics-for-nginx-oss)

panels.title: Requests/s
panels.description: All HTTP requests nginx served (static files, Django, probes, scrapes). Source: nginx_http_requests_total, nginx-prometheus-exporter README (https://github.com/nginx/nginx-prometheus-exporter#metrics-for-nginx-oss)

panels.title: Dropped connections
panels.description: Accepted minus handled connections per second: non-zero means nginx hit a resource limit (worker_connections). Source: nginx_connections_accepted / nginx_connections_handled, nginx-prometheus-exporter README (https://github.com/nginx/nginx-prometheus-exporter#metrics-for-nginx-oss)

panels.title: Queries and new connections
panels.description: Statements/s executed by Django (django_db_execute_total) and new DB connections/s (django_db_new_connections_total); a steady high connection rate means no connection reuse. Source: django-prometheus documentation/metrics.md (https://github.com/korfuri/django-prometheus/blob/master/documentation/metrics.md)

panels.title: Query duration p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: Django-side SQL duration, histogram django_db_query_duration_seconds. Source: django-prometheus documentation/metrics.md (https://github.com/korfuri/django-prometheus/blob/master/documentation/metrics.md)

panels.title: DB errors
panels.description: Execution errors by exception type (django_db_errors_total) and failed connection attempts (django_db_new_connection_errors_total). Both exist only after the first error (empty = none). Source: django-prometheus documentation/metrics.md (https://github.com/korfuri/django-prometheus/blob/master/documentation/metrics.md)

panels.title: Celery queue depth
panels.description: Length of the Valkey list `celery` (redis_key_size, REDIS_EXPORTER_CHECK_SINGLE_KEYS=db0=celery). Grows while imports are queued faster than the worker runs them; absent when empty. PENDING SCRAPE until the helm-charts/defectdojo change is synced.

panels.title: Clients
panels.description: Connected clients (uwsgi, celery worker and beat, exporter) and clients blocked on BRPOP (idle Celery workers waiting for tasks). Source: redis_connected_clients, redis_blocked_clients, redis_exporter (oliver006/redis_exporter v1.93.0, metrics from Valkey INFO).

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Valkey used memory and the container memory limit (maxmemory is 0 = no Valkey limit, policy noeviction: when the container limit is reached Valkey is OOM-killed). Source: redis_memory_used_bytes, kube-state-metrics.

panels.title: Commands and rejected connections
panels.description: Commands/s processed (redis_commands_processed_total) and connections rejected because of maxclients (redis_rejected_connections_total; awesome-prometheus-alerts (https://github.com/samber/awesome-prometheus-alerts) 'Redis rejected connections'). Source: redis_exporter (oliver006/redis_exporter v1.93.0, metrics from Valkey INFO).

panels.title: Memory: working set vs limit
panels.description: cAdvisor working set per container of the defectdojo namespace (uwsgi, nginx, celery worker and beat, valkey, postgres, exporters) and the memory limit (kube-state-metrics).

panels.title: CPU by container
panels.description: cAdvisor CPU cores per container. The Celery worker spikes during imports and deduplication.
